title: Sweeteners
subtitle: Not sugar. But not neutral either.
description: Sweeteners add sweetness with little or no energy. Non-sugar sweeteners and sugar alcohols are different categories with different criteria.
why_body: WHO advised in 2023 against using non-sugar sweeteners for weight control. The recommendation is conditional and is not a safety assessment. It does not apply to sugar alcohols such as sorbitol, maltitol, xylitol and erythritol, which the guideline explicitly excludes.
what_body: BOTIA detects non-sugar sweeteners — aspartame, acesulfame K, sucralose, saccharin, cyclamates, advantame, neotame, steviol glycosides — and separately, sugar alcohols, which provide energy and fall under different criteria.
can_1: Detect non-sugar sweeteners declared on the label.
can_2: Flag sugar alcohols that may cause digestive effects in large quantities.
can_3: Signal when a 'sugar-free' product contains multiple sweeteners.
cannot_1: Tell you whether sweeteners are safe for you personally.
cannot_2: Quantify your daily sweetener intake or cumulative exposure.
closing: If you are monitoring sweetener intake, check both the ingredient list and the nutrition label.
